title: Selected TESS CPVs have nearly equal harmonic change rates, unlike small longitude diffusion
abstract: We test whether small, continuous longitude diffusion can explain short-term changes in released TESS complex periodic variable (CPV) models. We compare noise-corrected complex structure functions for matched Fourier orders 3-5 and 8-12. In 45 visits of 24 selected stars, the ratio of median high-order to low-order change at one window lag is 1.45, with a 95% star-bootstrap interval of 0.41-2.45. The small-diffusion prediction is about 5.09. Brownian phase injections with window averaging give 5.04, while common-amplitude injections give 1.05. A paired spectral contrast stays below the diffusion reference without noise subtraction, with stricter signal cuts, and when selection uses earlier windows. Doubling formal errors makes corrected changes negative, so no physical ratio is assigned. We also show that clump replacement, whole-template uniform phase resets and common amplitude changes can all give order-independent change rates. The evidence weighs against small longitude diffusion as the sole source of change in these selected products. It does not identify replacement or measure material life. Selection, coefficient error assumptions, fixed injection masks and the lack of raw-cadence injections limit the inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, exact input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included.

display.caption: Matched low and high harmonic changes in 24 selected stars, and paired contrasts under noise and selection variants. The result tests small longitude diffusion, with stated coefficient and sampling assumptions.

citations.reason: Source of verified short-window harmonic coefficients and visit metadata. We test a temporal spectrum without tracking dip minima.
Tests inter-sector phase smearing; the present test concerns within-visit order dependence.
